reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 14.2 grants only a revocable, non-transferable licence to Customer alone that lapses with the Order Form term — it fails the fallback (no Affiliate coverage, no successor transferability) and sits in walk-away territory (revocable at Vendor's discretion, Affiliates/contractors excluded). Sections 13.1–13.3 do not cure it because they address the hosted Services licence, not Deliverables.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it adds Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, removes at-will revocability (tying revocation to the negotiated Section 13.3 standard), makes the paid-up Deliverable licence perpetual, and adds Affiliate/successor transferability — squarely the preferred position. Vendor's ownership of Deliverables is preserved, so the edit does not overreach on IP title.

The 0.832 changed-character ratio is acceptable here: the original sentence's revocability and Order-Form-term limits cannot be fixed by insertion alone, so replacing the licence sentence is the minimum route to the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the sensible fallback of aligning with Sections 13.2/13.3.

Minor points to tidy (not disqualifying): the added rights to "reproduce, display, modify, and create derivative works" go slightly beyond what the rule requires (scope of use is not a LICENSE parameter) and may draw resistance; and "perpetual, irrevocable ... revocable only as permitted by Section 13.3" is internally inconsistent — consider "perpetual and irrevocable except as permitted by Section 13.3."
